scope: Fifteen purposively selected cases spanning all five initial model cause categories; original metrics and quotations checked, including temporal anchoring errors.

updates.cause_explanation: All three retained sources were snippet fallbacks with download failures. Truncated manufacturing and cost quotations cannot establish specific 2026 exposure. An exemption reported in another cached source is not proof that these original snippets were false.

The selected evidence describes a March 2025 tariff threat and planned implementation. It does not establish the requested current component-level exposure. Differing source dates or product exemptions are not themselves demonstrated contradictions.

All five original extracted claims concern general critical-mineral trade policy and export controls, not import duties for the specified recycled lithium, nickel, and cobalt materials. Zero selected claims does not prove an extraction failure when the retrieved evidence is off topic. The requested relevance category includes this product-scope mismatch.

Historical classification examples and different product configurations do not establish a uniform current classification for automotive aluminum castings. References to 2025 are historical at the September 2026 audit date, not future policy. Different product classifications are not automatically contradictory.

The eleven extracted claims concern general metals tariffs, solar/wind applications, marine products, and trade agreements, without establishing Section 232 coverage for the specified EV battery trays/enclosures. The proposed recovery passages concern aluminum-extrusion antidumping investigation scope, which is a different trade-remedy program. Zero selected claims does not demonstrate synthesis failure: all eleven were supplied to synthesis. Product/program relevance is the principal observed gap.

Selected quotations describe statewide business costs and a 2025 national metals-tariff timeline, without named Georgia stamping-company import costs. March/August 2025 and April/July 2026 are historical at the September 2026 audit date. Different dated measures are not themselves conflicting evidence.

The display vendor discusses 2024/early-2025 potential reinstatement, tariff-list inclusion at times, and classification-dependent ranges. These are historical or conditional reports at the September 2026 audit date; exact TFT module classification, exclusion, and current Section 301 applicability remain unestablished. The 2024/2025 references are not future dates.

The selected vendor evidence gives an unquantified high-exposure assessment and conflates upstream export-quota risk with import-duty exposure. Older cached rulings and origin-specific rates cannot establish one current NMC cathode duty without matching product and origin. References to 2025/early-2026 measures are historical at this audit date, not future.

The original evidence includes September 2024 investigations and December 2025 AD orders, with product scope and exporter/country tables. These dates describe historical stages, not future initiation dates. A usable automotive CORE duty still requires matching the product, country, exporter, entry date and separate AD/CVD columns; current status is not independently checked. A named company is not required merely to answer the general policy question.
